title: Streamlined Toolflow + SDK Handoff Playbook (WIP)
summary: Working playbook describing a compact, incremental surface for tool-invoking streaming calls on the Hosted API and pragmatic SDK handoff patterns to enable gradual adoption across client libraries.
goals: Provide a minimal, expressive streaming contract for tool calls and structured results that reduces client complexity
Define SDK ergonomics (Python/TS/Go) that make resume, backpressure, and partial-output easy for developers
Offer an incremental rollout path so partners can opt into typed tool handshakes without breaking existing sessions
Surface telemetry and QoS signals (client- and server-side) to inform fallbacks and developer guidance
non_goals: Formal RFC for wire-level binary framing (we keep this textual/JSON-first for now)
Finalized schema language for every domain (we provide examples and versioning guidance)
Replacing existing advanced streaming SDK features—this is an approachable baseline
success_metrics: Reduction in customer-reported integration issues with streaming tool calls by 40% in first quarter after rollout
Average time-to-first-successful-tool-call for SDK users drops from 3 days to <24 hours
10% fewer developer support tickets related to partial-response resume and tool idempotency
Observed fallback-to-non-streaming rate for tool-heavy workloads <5% under normal conditions
constraints: Must work within existing Hosted API auth and rate-limiting semantics
Should be backwards-compatible with current incremental JSON streaming responses
Keep server CPU/memory overhead modest—avoid heavyweight per-session state unless pinned by enterprise Dedicated customers
Mobile/edge clients can reasonably implement the SDK surface without large binary deps
proposed_design: Core idea: a three-tier execution surface built on top of existing incremental streaming. 1) Lightweight 'partial-frames', a compact JSON frame suitable for progressive text and small structured fields; 2) 'tool-handshake' frames, a typed but optional negotiation channel to request tool execution and receive resolved outputs; 3) 'session-resume' markers. The server emits atomic frames (delta text, structured result, tool-invocation-request, tool-result, checkpoint). Clients can choose to parse only text deltas, or fully participate in tool handshakes. Handshakes are opt-in and versioned via a "protocol_version" field. When a client advertises support, the server will emit higher-fidelity tool frames; otherwise it degrades to plain-text descriptions of the same action. This keeps old clients functional while enabling richer SDK features.
streaming_handshake: Minimal fields for handshake frame: {"protocol_version": "1.0", "session_id": "uuid", "capabilities": ["tool-invoke", "resume", "prefetch-summaries"]}. Server side: on handshake, server replies with a session manifest that lists currently-available tool variants (id, latency-profile, cost-tier) and recommended fallback model ids. Handshake is authenticated with the same API token; per-tenant isolation is preserved. If the handshake fails, server falls back to annotated text-only guidance (e.g., "To perform action X call external service Y with params Z").
tool_call_semantics: Tool invocation model: tool-call frames contain 'tool_id', 'inputs', 'idempotency_key', and 'expected_contract' (optional typed schema reference). Tool results are returned as separate frames with 'tool_result' (structured JSON), 'status' (success|error|timeout), and optional 'confidence' (float). Important implementation notes: - Tool calls are 'requesting' from the LLM's plan; the server must mediate timeouts and retries. - Clients must honor idempotency_key to avoid double-actuation. - Servers should emit 'tool-queue-position' for long-running tool executions so clients can display progress.
structured_output_and_schema_versioning: Approach: encourage narrow per-action schemas (JSON Schema or a small typed stencil) rather than a single global model. Each schema carries a stable id and semantic version (e.g., 'todo:action:create:1.2'). Server supports 'schema_preview' in session manifest for clients to pre-validate. Schema upgrades: server emits 'deprecated' flags and 'migrations' in manifest; SDKs provide a 'strict' vs 'lenient' parse option. For backward compatibility, tool results should include both 'structured' and 'verbose_text' fields when possible.
sdk_guidelines: Handshake-once-per-session: establish capabilities early and cache manifest for route-scoped reuse
Expose a single high-level 'call' primitive that returns an async iterator over frames (text deltas, tool events, checkpoints)
Provide helper to reconstruct full text from deltas for clients that need transcripts
Offer built-in idempotency utilities and simple retry policies for tool calls
Default SDK mode: 'lenient' parse + structured when available; opt-in 'strict' mode for safety-sensitive customers
Mobile SDKs: prefer coalesced frames and include a prefetch hint to reduce wakeups
client_backpressure_and_resume: Backpressure: server advertises a 'preferred_token_rate' in the manifest; client SDKs should expose hooks to honor or ignore with a clear warning. Resume: periodic 'checkpoint' frames record last-acknowledged offset and included KV of 'partial_state' (compact). To resume: client reopens stream with 'resume_from' and 'session_id' + proof-of-possession header. For low-trust networks, we provide a 'compact transcript' blob that can be re-sent if the live ephemeral resume fails.
telemetry_and_observability: Minimum telemetry emitted by SDKs: handshake latency, frames_received, frames_parsed, tool_calls_initiated, tool_call_latency, resume_attempts, fallback_count. Server-side: per-session CPU, queue_time, tool_queue_metrics, model-variant chosen, and per-frame serialization sizes. All telemetry maps to existing Console dashboards; add a new 'streaming-toolflow' dashboard with per-route heatmaps and sample traces.
migration_and_rollout: Phased approach: 1) server-side: add manifest and emit annotated text-only frames (no SDK changes needed); 2) lightweight SDK updates: parse manifest and expose passive helpers (non-breaking); 3) opt-in beta: enable tool handshake for whitelisted customers and collect metrics; 4) wider rollout with feature-flagged enforcement of idempotency and resume helpers. Default remains backward-compatible: if client doesn't support handshake, text-only fallbacks are sufficient.
security_and_safety_considerations: Tool calls may perform sensitive actuation: require explicit enterprise policy toggles, per-tool allowlists, and KMS-backed audit logs. SDKs should treat tool-result structured payloads as untrusted and encourage validation against declared schema. Servers must rate-limit tool invocations separately and surface cost implications to clients.
examples: Example streamed sequence (high-level): 1) Client: open stream + handshake(capabilities=[tool-invoke,resume]) 2) Server: manifest with tools: [{id:'search',latency:'100ms'},{id:'run-code',latency:'5s'}] 3) Server: text_delta 'Ok I will search for X' 4) Server: tool_request(tool_id:'search', inputs:{q:'X'}, idempotency_key:'k1') 5) Server: tool_result(tool_id:'search', structured:{results:[...]}, status:'success') 6) Server: text_delta 'Found 3 results, summarizing...' 7) Server: checkpoint(offset:345, partial_state:{summary:'...'})
open_questions: Do we need a formal schema registry vs. embedding schema blobs in manifest?
Should tool_result include signed metadata for high-assurance actuation auditing?
What's the recommended TTL for cached manifests in mobile clients?
How aggressively should server coalesce small frames vs. emitting many tiny deltas?
